PART 2 IS THE UPDATE ON THE SEDATION NEGLIGENCE CASE.

CLEAR AND CATEGORICAL CLARIFICATION: Although the incident occurred at the Jaime el Conquistador clinic, the negligent veterinarian was María, who works at both clinics.

1. THEY KILLED MY CAT! A healthy 2-year-old cat arrived with a fecal impaction. She had already undergone the same procedure several times with other veterinarians there. Yesterday, I had a new cat vet visit. It was 7:00 PM, and because they rushed the procedure, they overdid the anesthesia and/or perforated her intestine. They told me it was normal and that she would wake up, until she went into cardiac arrest and nothing could be done. Furthermore, they didn't run any blood tests before sedation; they didn't know her oxygen saturation or blood sugar levels. These women are negligent; they ruined a healthy cat. I understand they want to go home and rest, but you don't play with a life. The so-called veterinarian who treated my cat is María, so be very careful if this woman ruins your cats. The assistant left looking like things had been done wrong, and this woman, without a shred of empathy, said everything was fine.

María: You should have seen my cat convulsing because of your negligence and lack of professionalism.

2. The veterinarians at this center, as expected, have not taken responsibility. The "veterinarian," Alejandro, presumably the one in charge, said that the cat was in perfect condition when she left the clinic. I have photos and videos from two different days of the same procedure, and the cat didn't come out the same. Please, for the love you have for your pets, do not go to this veterinary clinic.

This same individual told me that to perform a dental cleaning on my cat, they would first sedate him, and then, once sedated, they would do blood work to see how the cat was doing. You don't need to be a veterinarian, or particularly bright, to know that pre-operative procedures are necessary before anesthesia. In short, my cat will not be returning, but your cats will not fall into the hands of these people.

ANSWER: Indeed, the kitten had a chronic condition, which had already been treated at your clinic many times by other veterinarians (Carmen and Lidia). They always performed blood tests to determine if they could euthanize her. On September 4th, when María saw her, at 7:30 PM, apparently, being a rather irresponsible person, she decided to administer sedation without checking on the kitten's condition. Furthermore, as you yourself say, we have photos and videos of other procedures and of the one performed by María the day she killed her. Lina appeared completely different from how she usually did; she didn't appear drugged, she appeared alert and meowing.
We called you several times, Alejandro, to ask about Lina's condition, and you didn't answer a single call. I suppose it's because that incompetent woman had already told you that she had done something wrong and that Lina was going to die. Besides, in that call you just had with my mom (very subtle, by the way), it was already pointed out to you that it's the vet's responsibility to say that if Lina is still drugged or whatever in an hour, she should be taken to the emergency room, because guess what? WE ARE NOT VETERINARIANS. That's clear negligence on Maria's part, which the veterinary association will have to investigate. Even if it's Friday night and Maria works with LIVES, if she was tired, she could have said we should go the next day to have Lina seen, but what difference does it make, right? One more life, one less life, they're not your pets anyway.

The fact is, Lina entered your clinic alive and well, and leaving there was a death sentence for her. I completely stand by my accusations against the negligent vet and your clinic.
Very good clinic with long opening hours

I'm going to euthanize a 25-kilo, 17-year-old dog. I've already discussed everything with Gabi: the price, the procedure, etc. When I arrive, there's another vet there, I think she's Venezuelan. They don't even call me to let me know Gabi isn't there for something so intimate and painful. This other woman tells me that "as per protocol" she has to do blood work, 60 euros, and that she'll have the results in 20 minutes. I leave because I think she just wants to rip me off and, on top of that, give a dog a shot. I've had other blood tests done there before, and they would take the blood to another place for analysis. It all seems very, very strange. I'm not going back! The previous vets, whom I suppose they fired, were fantastic! Marga and Borja were excellent! I know for a fact that I'm not the first client they've lost! What values ​​will a 17-year-old, large dog have in a blood test...because he weighed 40 kilos and is now at 25! Vet Borja and Vet Marga were fantastic!! Excellent!!
They are all so lovely! They treat my cats with so much care, and we are truly delighted to have found our trusted clinic.

Unfortunately, I have to confirm what other users of this clinic have said.

Since the veterinarians changed, the quality of diagnoses has worsened considerably. It's clear they're inexperienced and don't seem very motivated to work.
In my case, and they know who I am, I've been going for years until yesterday. I tried to give them a chance because everyone has a first time, but they messed up, and she knows who she is. Coco came to the clinic feeling unwell because he couldn't tolerate the anti-inflammatory medication they prescribed, but his subsequent corticosteroid treatment worsened his condition, causing bloody diarrhea that same afternoon. I called and sent photos of his stool; they replied two hours later.
Within two hours, I left another clinic with an accurate diagnosis. Twenty-four hours have passed, and Coco is back to his old self, a far cry from the three days of discomfort and pain he endured due to the misdiagnosis.
I'm not a veterinarian; I didn't study to be one.

You did, but I see it didn't do much good.

I hope the clinic owner thinks carefully about what kind of professionals treat his furry clients.
You don't need to reply to this comment now; it's unnecessary. You needed to when I sent you the photos.

And stop prescribing corticosteroids indiscriminately; they have side effects. Don't go around saying that with these doses "nothing will happen." First, get a proper diagnosis, and then say it's fine; that's the correct order.

Anyway, just so you know, Coco probably has chronic pancreatitis. I warned him that same day, asking if we could examine his pancreas, and he told me that the ultrasound from two months ago showed nothing abnormal... Anyway.
It's not worth going into more detail.
You don't deserve my energy; you just want to make money.
